text:
Jane Doe (Customer): Hi, our app hit quota mid-month and the customer is asking when the monthly credits actually refill. They drained tokens yesterday at ~23:30 in their local PST. Do we reset by customer timezone or do we use a global reset?

Sara (Support): Good q — we default to a single global reset. It should be at 00:00 UTC on the 1st of the month. So PST customers see it on the previous day (16:00 PST).

Jane Doe (Customer): Ah ok. The customer insists they still show 0 credits after midnight local time. Could the reset take a bit to run?

Tom (Billing): There can be a small propagation delay. The scheduled reset job runs at 00:00 UTC and most accounts update within a few minutes. If they still see 0 after ~10min, refresh the Console and try the usage export.

Jane Doe (Customer): What should I ask them to send if it doesn’t refresh?

Sara (Support): Ask for (1) account ID, (2) screenshot of billing page showing 0, (3) approximate local time they observed the zero-state, and (4) a CSV export from the Usage tab if possible. That covers timezones and verifies no duplicate charges.

Raj (Infra): For reproducibility, also ask them to clear cache or open an incognito window. The Console caches a bit of UI state; the backend counters are correct sooner than the UI always reflects it.

Tom (Billing): Note: if they have a monthly committed plan vs pay-as-you-go, refill semantics differ. Reserved/Dedicated customers have committed capacity and don't see "credits" top up — capacity is persistent. This thread sounds like pay-as-you-go credits.

Jane Doe (Customer): They were on the free monthly credits grant. Is that different?

Sara (Support): Free credits behave like regular monthly credits and reset on 00:00 UTC as well. No special timezone exemption.

Raj (Infra): If they report requests still 429-ing after the reset, ask for a sample error response. Typical 429 looks like:

```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "error": "rate_limit_exceeded",
  "message": "monthly quota exhausted",
  "retry_after": 3600
}
```

If the Retry-After header is present, clients should honor it. The platform will not automatically allow more tokens until the quota window resets or extra credits are purchased.

Tom (Billing): If they need immediate capacity while we investigate, recommend a short-term top-up or upgrading to a paid plan. For one-offs we can add credits manually if you include the account ID and justification.

Jane Doe (Customer): Any automated pro-rata or mid-month top-ups? They expected some pro-rata refill after upgrading mid-cycle.

Tom (Billing): Upgrades can trigger pro-rated billing, but token grant increases from a plan change take effect immediately for paid plans only. The free monthly grants do not pro-rate. If they upgraded from free to paid mid-month, they should see new paid quota added instantly in the Console; if not, we should escalate.

Sara (Support): Repro steps we give to customers: 1) Check Console > Billing > Usage and refresh. 2) If zero persists, download CSV export for the last 7 days. 3) Attempt a single lightweight API call to confirm 429 and copy the full response headers/body. 4) If they upgraded, include the invoice/confirmation email timestamp.

Raj (Infra): For internal triage, include the account ID so we can check backend counters and job run logs around 00:00 UTC. We can look for delayed reset job runs or queuing issues. If the job ran late, we note it and communicate ETA to customer.

Jane Doe (Customer): Thanks — I’ll ask for the account ID + CSV + any 429 payloads and report back.

billing-bot: Automated note: monthly_quota_reset job completed at 2026-02-01T00:00:12Z for shard 3 (status: success) :white_check_mark: (reaction :eyes:)

Tom (Billing): If you get that bot log matching the account's shard and they still see 0 after UI refresh, ping me and I’ll open a billing ticket to apply a manual top-up while infra investigates.

Sara (Support): Great — loop back here when you have artifacts and we’ll escalate as needed. :thumbsup:
